newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan police arrest 15 in investment scheme.
newsitem.headline: Japan police arrest 15 in investment scheme.

text.p: Japanese police on Monday arrested a Tokyo businessman on suspicion of fraud in what investigators said was a pyramid-style investment scheme that cheated 10 investors out of 100 million yen ($826,000).

Ichiro Yamamoto, chairman of the Keizai Kaikaku Club (KKC), was arrested along with 14 other club officials, including his wife, after investigations that began last June with a raid on the club's Tokyo headquarters, police said.
KKC, established in May 1995, collected 35 billion yen ($289 million) from some 12,000 people on promises they would receive huge dividends, police said.
The flamboyant Yamamoto, who according to media reports recruited investors with an almost religious fervour, has denied the fraud accusations against him.

"I had no intention of cheating investors," Yamamoto told reporters on Monday. "We intend to do business with the invested money and pay interest, but because of the police raid, we were forced to stop our business."
